style_anaphora.coling::a0b0f9d5-62dc-4996-9de4-5e5f9b3b: This review notes that the paper introduces Edward, a probabilistic programming language built over TensorFlow and Python, supporting a broad suite of modern probabilistic machine learning techniques. This review notes that the Edward library provides an exceptionally impressive collection of modern probabilistic inference methods within an accessible and easily usable software package. This review notes that the paper offers a brief review of key techniques from a representation learning perspective, combined with two experiments evaluating variational inference and GPU accelerated Hybrid Monte Carlo. This review notes that the first experiment on variational inference would be far more valuable if the authors provided a clear link to complete reproducible code. This review notes that the Hybrid Monte Carlo experiment looks acceptable, except that characterizing Stan as a hand-optimized implementation seems unfair, as the Stan code was clearly not hand-optimized for this specific model and hardware setup. This review notes that no one seriously doubts the high quality of the implementation, so the authors should avoid undermining the submission with unsubstantiated sensationalist claims. This review notes that instead of focusing on drama, the authors should compare head-to-head against Stan on a single CPU core while separately reporting speedups gained from parallelization and GPU hardware. This review notes that these detailed performance numbers would help readers accurately estimate the performance of the proposed method across alternative hardware configurations. This review notes that the manuscript is generally clearly written and quite easy for the target audience to read. This review notes that while the code examples are helpful, they are also somewhat difficult to interpret because it is occasionally unclear what context is missing. This review notes that it would be extremely helpful if the authors provided a clear link to a machine-readable companion, such as a Jupyter notebook or plain text file, containing complete runnable code for all presented examples. This review notes that the Edward library clearly represents a unique collection of powerful probabilistic inference methods. This review notes that the primary threat to the novelty of this paper stems from previous publications by the exact same research group. This review notes that the main text explicitly references Tran et al. (2016a), which covers a lot of similar material from a slightly different perspective. This review notes that it remains unclear whether that related paper has been published or submitted somewhere else. This review notes that Edward will very likely have a profound and lasting impact on the fields of Bayesian machine learning and deep learning. This review notes that drawing a rigid distinction in Section 2 between specialized languages like Stan and Turing-complete languages like Edward seems unfair, given that Stan is also Turing-complete. This review notes that the authors provide no technical proof to support their explicit assertion regarding the Turing-completeness of Edward.
style_anaphora.coling::d8e4451f-f606-413a-a2c5-5f2b5e9c: I must note that this paper is exceptionally long, stretching to seventeen pages without even including any supplementary material. I must note that while ICLR does not have an official page limit, authors ought to put themselves in the reviewer's shoes and avoid taking undue advantage of this open rule. I must note that having one or two pages in addition to the conventional eight-page limit is acceptable, but more than doubling the length is quite unfair. I must note that turning to the actual review, the paper proposes a new artificial dataset designed for sequence learning. I must note that I call this dataset artificial because it was synthetically generated from the original MNIST dataset, which is a smallish dataset of real handwritten digit images. I must note that in addition to the dataset, the authors propose to train recurrent networks using a schedule over the sequence length, which they term incremental learning. I must note that their experiments show that the proposed schedule performs better than having no schedule at all on this dataset. I must note that the authors furthermore demonstrate that their schedule outperforms several other intuitive schedules. I must note that the authors verify these findings by conducting ablation studies on the model using the proposed dataset. I must note that I have several critical issues with this paper that must be highlighted. I must note that I did not find anything novel in the core methodology of this paper. I must note that the proposed incremental learning schedule is nothing new and represents a natural thing to try when learning sequence models. I must note that similar ideas have already been explored by multiple authors, including Bengio in 2015 and Ranzato in 2015. I must note that the only truly new piece of work is the set of ablation studies conducted to verify that performance gains stem from the curriculum. I must note that the authors only test their hypothesis on a single dataset that they proposed and artificially generated. I must note that one must ask why they did not use a real sequential dataset, such as language modeling. I must note that one naturally wonders whether the technique simply fails to work in that real-world scenario. I must note that I am positive that for language modeling with huge vocabulary sizes, performance gains will be nowhere near the seventy-four percent reported here. I must note that I am not convinced about the actual value of introducing this artificial dataset. I must note that many real-world sequential datasets already exist across domains like text, speech, finance, and other fields. I must note that what exactly this dataset brings to the table is not super clear to me. I must note that while having another dataset is fine, I felt this dataset was created solely to make the proposed ideas work. In this paper, we introduce the binary value principle, which is a simple subset-sum instance expressing the basic fact that a natural number written in binary notation cannot be negative, and we relate this principle directly to central problems in proof complexity and algebraic complexity.

In this paper, we prove conditional superpolynomial lower bounds on the Ideal Proof System refutation size of this instance, based on a well-known hypothesis by Shub and Smale concerning the hardness of computing factorials, where the Ideal Proof System is the strong algebraic proof system introduced by Grochow and Pitassi.

In this paper, we show conversely that short Ideal Proof System refutations of this instance bridge the gap between sufficiently strong algebraic and semi-algebraic proof systems.

In this paper, we extend to the full-fledged Ideal Proof System the paradigm introduced by Forbes et al., whereby lower bounds against subsystems of the Ideal Proof System were obtained using restricted algebraic circuit lower bounds.

In this paper, we demonstrate that the binary value principle captures the distinct advantage of semi-algebraic over algebraic reasoning for sufficiently strong systems.

In this paper, we show that the Shub-Smale hypothesis implies a superpolynomial lower bound on the size of Ideal Proof System refutations of the binary value principle over the rational numbers, defined as the unsatisfiable linear equation summing powers of two with boolean variables to equal negative one.

In this paper, we show that the related tau-conjecture implies a superpolynomial lower bound on the size of Ideal Proof System refutations of a variant of the binary value principle over the ring of rational functions.

In this paper, we note that no prior conditional lower bounds were known for the Ideal Proof System or for apparently much weaker propositional proof systems such as Frege.

In this paper, we observe that although simple, the binary value principle is not a direct translation of a boolean formula, so Ideal Proof System lower bounds on this principle do not necessarily entail lower bounds for Frege or its subsystems.

In this paper, we show that admitting short refutations of the binary value principle is necessary for any algebraic proof system to fully simulate any known semi-algebraic proof system, and for sufficiently strong algebraic proof systems it is also sufficient.

In this paper, we introduce a very strong proof system that simulates all known semi-algebraic proof systems under the name Cone Proof System, serving as a semi-algebraic analogue of the Ideal Proof System that establishes unsatisfiability of polynomial equalities and inequalities over the reals by representing sum-of-squares proofs as algebraic circuits.

In this paper, we prove that the Ideal Proof System is polynomially equivalent to the Cone Proof System if and only if the Ideal Proof System admits polynomial-size refutations of the binary value principle over both the integers and the rational numbers.

It is recorded that Corfe Castle railway station is a railway station located in the village of Corfe Castle, in the English county of Dorset. It is recorded that originally an intermediate station on the London and South Western Railway branch line from Wareham to Swanage, the line and station were closed by British Rail in 1972. It is recorded that the station has since reopened as a station on the Swanage Railway, a heritage railway that runs from Norden station just north of Corfe Castle to Swanage station. It is recorded that Corfe Castle is on a railway line connecting Wareham and Norden.

It is recorded that Corfe Castle lies in the centre of the Isle of Purbeck, a peninsula bordered by the English Channel to the south, and by the marshy lands of the River Frome and Poole Harbour to the north and east. It is recorded that in the early nineteenth century, the area around Corfe Castle was known for Purbeck Ball Clay, shipped by horse-drawn tramways—the Middlebere Plateway and Furzebrook Railway—to wharves on Poole Harbour. It is recorded that the port of Swanage at the tip of the Isle of Purbeck was equally well known for the Purbeck Marble that was mined locally and shipped out by sea.

It is recorded that the presence of these industries attracted railway promoters once the London and South Western Railway main line reached Wareham in 1847. It is recorded that several schemes were promoted and failed, but eventually the Swanage Railway received its Act of Parliament in 1881 and opened on 20 May 1885. It is recorded that the position of Corfe Castle, commanding the only relatively low level route across the hilly spine of the Isle of Purbeck, meant the line passed close to the village centre, and the station was built for its opening. It is recorded that from its opening, the line was operated by the London and South Western Railway, and the line was absorbed into that railway in 1886. It is recorded that Corfe Castle station was the only intermediate station on the Swanage branch until closure, possessing the only passing loop between Worgret Junction and Swanage.

It is recorded that at least one camping coach was positioned here by the Southern Region from 1954 to 1967, and probably from 1948 to 1953. It is recorded that from 1960, the allocated coach was a camping coach converted from a Pullman car, which was fitted with a full kitchen, two sleeping compartments, and a room with two single beds. It is recorded that from 1962 until 1967 there were two of these coaches here.

It is recorded that while the development of Swanage as a tourist resort brought additional passenger traffic to the line, the collapse of both the clay and marble industries, and the increase in private car ownership in the second half of the twentieth century made the line unprofitable. It is recorded that closure was first proposed in 1967, and despite local opposition the line finally closed on 3 January 1972. It is recorded that during the final few years of the line's operation under British Rail, passenger train services were operated by two-car Class 205 diesel electric multiple units, also known as type 2H.

It is recorded that from the time of the first proposal of closure, a campaign to reopen the railway as a steam locomotive operated heritage railway developed. It is recorded that most of the track bed, including Corfe Castle station, was bought by Dorset County Council. It is recorded that proposals to use the railway route through the Corfe Castle gap as a road bypass for the village were eventually rejected by the county council in 1986. It is recorded that in the meantime the Swanage Railway had started operating a steam service at the Swanage end of the line in 1982.

It is recorded that there were concerns that reopening Corfe Castle station as a northern terminus for the Swanage Railway would cause parking problems in the village. It is recorded that it was therefore decided to extend the line a further half a mile north to a new Park and Ride site built on the former location of the exchange sidings between the Swanage branch and the clay tramways. It is recorded that here the new Norden station was built and most trains terminate here. It is recorded that Corfe Castle station reopened on 12 August 1995, although the official opening was not until February of the following year.

It is recorded that a five-year project by Swanage Railway volunteers to install a footbridge across the running lines between the platforms at Corfe Castle was completed in April 2007, when David Quarmby, CBE, carried out the official opening. It is recorded that the footbridge was originally built in 1893 by the London, Brighton and South Coast Railway. It is recorded that with cast-iron columns and a wrought iron span, the footbridge spent its life at Merton Park in London, near Wimbledon, on the West Croydon line until removed by Swanage Railway volunteers. It is recorded that the footbridge can accommodate the people who now use Corfe Castle station, and is safer and more convenient for the public than crossing over the track via the gated and locked foot crossing. It is recorded that the project won the National Railway Heritage Awards in December 2007, with a plaque presented to engineer Philip Wycliffe-Jones and his volunteer team by Gwyneth Dunwoody, Chairman of the Transport Select Committee.

It is recorded that in summer 2018 and 2019 South Western Railway operated two trains per day to and from Wareham, one of which continued to Poole and the other to London Waterloo via Weymouth. It is recorded that National Rail weekend services operated between Wareham and Swanage in summer 2018 and 2019, run by West Coast Railway Company with three daily trains per direction. It is recorded that however, in July 2019 these services were stopped and there are currently no National Rail services to Corfe Castle.

It is recorded that services run every day from the beginning of April to late October, with weekend only operation in March, November and December. It is recorded that the level of service varies from six to seventeen trains a day in each direction, depending on the season and the day of the week. It is recorded that northbound, trains operate to Norden station in three minutes.

It is recorded that Corfe Castle station is also the home of the Swanage Railway's Railway Museum, which is housed in the old goods shed and an adjacent rail van. It is recorded that the museum is open on most operating days.

It is recorded that the museum includes Secundus, a narrow gauge steam locomotive built by Bellis and Seeking in 1874 for the nearby Furzebrook Railway. It is recorded that this locomotive was in use until 1955, and then displayed in the now defunct Birmingham Museum of Science and Industry until 2000. It is recorded that it is planned that the locomotive will eventually be transferred to a new home at the Purbeck Mineral and Mining Museum, currently being developed adjacent to Norden railway station.

style_anaphora.coling::9600c031-1ba2-4882-9aa0-8cb6b07d: It is known that Operation Claw was a joint Swedish-American operation, with Norwegian support, carried out at Lillehammer shortly after the German capitulation at the end of World War II. It is known that the intelligence material from Operation Claw, among it a Soviet codebook, became very useful for the Americans during the Cold War. It is known that Operation Claw was controversial both when it happened and afterwards. It is known that in 1945 it was controversial that the Americans operated in what was seen as a British controlled country. It is known that it was controversial that they secured information about their ally the Soviet Union, in cooperation with neutral Sweden. It is known that a hypothesis that Norwegian resistance fighter Kai Holst's sudden death in June 1945 was related to Operation Claw has been put forward by historian Tore Pryser. It is known that even before the war in Europe ended the various allied states had begun the search for German scientists and other German expertise. It is known that signals intelligence had been vital during World War II, especially British work breaking German codes from Enigma. It is known that the war was still fought in East Asia, the U.S. and Soviet Union were allies, and Americans counted on Soviet assistance against Japan. It is known that the allies had designated Norway as part of the British sphere of influence. It is known that both for the U.S. and neutral Sweden the operation was thus very sensitive and was conducted in great secrecy. It is known that in the Wehrmacht camp at Lillehammer a group of thirty-five German experts on signals intelligence were gathered. It is known that they had been working on the Eastern Front against Soviet forces and had an archive and extensive knowledge about Soviet affairs. It is known that this was knowledge the Western Allies, and especially the Americans, wanted and that probably were of use during the Cold War. It is known that in cooperation with the OSS and Norwegian legation, agents for Swedish C-byrån traveled with two Norwegian intelligence specialists to Lillehammer on May 9 and 10, 1945. It is known that the German group of experts were taken out of the camp and transported to Sweden. It is known that after a few weeks in Sweden they were on June 12 flown from Torslanda Airport close to Gothenburg to U.S. occupied Germany and interned in an American military camp at Wiesbaden. It is known that the transfer to Sweden of the German experts at Lillehammer, which OSS called Operation Claw, was directed from the highest level. It is known that from the U.S. side the leader of OSS, Major General William J. Donovan was involved. It is known that from the Swedish side the chief of the Defense Staff, Major General Carl August Ehrensvärd was involved. It is known that the famous Swedish police director Harry Söderman was also involved from the Swedish side. It is known that Kai Holst had been working at military office number 4 at the Norwegian legation in Stockholm, and after the search he unexpectedly traveled right back to Stockholm. It is known that the official cause of death was stated as suicide, but Holst's family and resistance colleagues believed he was liquidated. It is known that historian Tore Pryser put forward the hypothesis that Holst brought information from Lillehammer that could damage Operation Claw and was thus killed. It is known that to be able to damage the operation, Kai Holst cannot have been trusted as others were. It is known that he must have been considered a threat due to his contact with Alexandra Kollontaj who was ambassador in Stockholm representing the Soviet Union. It is known that a possible reason for a murder of Kai Holst was thus not his knowledge as such, but his connections. It is known that Operation Claw was the beginning of post-war cooperation between Swedish and U.S. intelligence services, in violation of Sweden's officially stated neutrality. It is known that from the American side the operation was viewed as a success, and OSS officers William T. Carlson and Joseph T. Kloman were honored with decorations. It is known that for Swedish C-byrån, Operation Claw quickly became toxic. It is known that even though the operation was to be kept confidential, information leaked to the Swedish press and C-byrån was dissolved in February 1946. It is known that information regarding Operation Claw continued to be classified as confidential in post-war years and some of it remains so today. It is known that a report about the operation in the British National Archives is restricted until 2020.
style_anaphora.coling::32e519e5-5c7c-4bcb-a0ea-bfeb2b47: In modern Greek art, the primary period under consideration spans the era between the emergence of the independent Greek state and the twentieth century. In modern Greek art, Greek islands such as Crete, and the Ionian islands in particular, were under Venetian or European rule for extended periods. In modern Greek art, these islands were consequently able to assimilate the radical artistic changes occurring across Europe during the fourteenth through eighteenth centuries. In modern Greek art, the Cretan School represents an important artistic movement that followed parallel routes to Western Europe. In modern Greek art, the Heptanese School of art stands as another important movement following parallel paths to Western Europe. In modern Greek art, creative development was predominantly shaped by national socioeconomic conditions, the widespread diaspora across Europe, and the new social elite. In modern Greek art, external artistic influences played a major role, arriving predominantly from Germany and France. In modern Greek art, sculpture and painting emerged as the primary domains of aesthetic expression. In modern Greek art, the nineteenth century represented a foundational period of stylistic development. In modern Greek art, the School of Munich became the dominant influence during the nineteenth century. In modern Greek art, development began around the period of Romanticism in Western Europe. In modern Greek art, Greek artists absorbed elements from European colleagues, resulting in a distinctive Greek Romantic style inspired by revolutionary ideals, local geography, and history. What can be stated about the studied two-dimensional model?
The studied two-dimensional model describes a topological crystalline insulator protected by rotation symmetry, built by stacking two Chern insulators with opposite Chern numbers transforming under conjugate representations of the rotation group.

What can be stated about surface states in this model?
Surface states in this model are not stable or gapless, despite similarities to the Kane-Mele model.

What can be stated about the topological responses of the model?
The topological responses of the model include quantized fractional charge bound to disclinations and angular momentum pumping when threading an elementary magnetic flux.

What can be stated about the theory describing these responses?
The theory describing these responses is a mutual Chern-Simons coupling between the electromagnetic gauge field and an effective gauge field for rotation symmetry.

What can be stated about the fragile topology of the filled bands?
The fragile topology of the filled bands means that while they lack a symmetric Wannier representation, this obstruction is removed by adding appropriate atomic orbitals.

What can be stated about the response of the model?
The response of the model can be derived by representing it as a superposition of atomic orbitals with positive and negative integer coefficients.

What can be stated about point-group TCIs lacking surface states?
Point-group TCIs lacking surface states are either atomic insulators or fragile phases.

Gapless surface states in free electron systems exist if and only if there is a stable Wannier obstruction.

The dimensional reduction mapping converts the two-dimensional rotation-protected classification to a zero-dimensional problem, yielding the complete non-interacting classification and its reduction under interactions.

What is known regarding the CII 158 microns line in galaxies? The CII 158 microns line in galaxies is the most important coolant of the interstellar medium, but substantial variations are seen from object to object. The main source of emission at a galactic scale is still poorly understood because previous studies have a resolution of several kpc, so the observed emission is an average of different ISM components.

What is known regarding the main aim of this work? The main aim of this work is to study, for the first time, the CII emission at the scale of a spiral arm. We investigate the origin of this line and its use as a tracer of star formation, presenting CII and OI observations of an M31 spiral arm segment using the Infrared Space Observatory.

What is known regarding the comparison of CII emission with other tracers? The comparison of CII emission with other tracers shows that similarity of CII emission with H-alpha and Spitzer 24 mu images is striking when smoothed to identical resolution, whereas the correlation with the neutral gas tracers CO and HI is much weaker.

What is known regarding the CII cooling rate per H atom? The CII cooling rate per H atom increases dramatically from ~2.7e-26 ergs/s/atom in the border of the map to ~1.4e-25 ergs/s/atom in the regions of star formation.

What is known regarding the CII/FIR ratio in M31? The CII/FIR ratio in M31 is almost constant at 2%, a factor 3 higher than typically quoted. However, M31 is not unusual because whole-galaxy fluxes used for comparisons include central regions where the ratio is lower, and resolved observations neither isolate a spiral arm nor include data as far out in the galactic disk.

What is known regarding PDR model fits for these regions? PDR model fits for these regions yield a plausible average solution of G_0~100 and n~3000 for the PDR emission in the regions of star formation in the arm of M31.

What is known about the baryon acoustic oscillation peak?
The baryon acoustic oscillation peak, observed in cosmic matter distributions at redshifts up to ~3.5, reflects the expansion of the sonic horizon identified in cosmic microwave background anisotropies.

What is known about the measurement precision of the BAO peak position?
The measurement precision of the BAO peak position is better than ~1% using galaxies, and ~1.4-1.6% using Ly-alpha forests and quasar clustering.

What is known about the diagnostic power of BAO with the Alcock-Paczynski effect?
The diagnostic power of BAO with the Alcock-Paczynski effect, which arises from changing ratios of angular to spatial size of spherically-symmetric distributions, makes it a powerful cosmological tool.

What is known about the empirical data utilized in this paper?
The empirical data utilized in this paper includes five BAO peak measurements from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV release at redshifts <z>=0.38, 0.51, 0.70, 1.48, and 2.33.

What is known about the primary model comparison performed here?
The primary model comparison performed here directly evaluates the standard Lambda-CDM model against the R_h=ct universe using both the Alcock-Paczynski diagnostic and a complementary volume-averaged distance probe.

What is known about the parameter dependence of these distance probes?
The parameter dependence of these distance probes is minimal, as both are free of uncertain parameters like the Hubble constant, fitting them ideally for model selection.

What is known about the probe-specific model selection results?
The probe-specific model selection results show R_h=ct favored by the AP effect (~75% versus ~25%), while Planck-Lambda-CDM is favored by the volume-averaged probe (~80% versus ~20%).

What is known about the overall outcome of this study?
The overall outcome of this study is inconclusive under a joint analysis, failing to confirm that BAO data alone support an accelerating Universe.

What is the problem regarding the immense size of the Atlantic Ocean?
The immense size of the Atlantic Ocean creates a major obstacle because the sea is so vast that it can be wider than the entire United States depending on where you cross. Driving across such a massive expanse would be extremely boring, and vehicles would be unable to carry enough fuel for the trip unless fuel were shipped to stations in the middle of the ocean, which completely defeats the purpose of driving.

What is the problem regarding deep ocean pilings for an Atlantic bridge?
Deep ocean pilings for an Atlantic bridge present a major technical challenge because the water is far too deep to sink pilings down to the seabed. Without pilings anchored into the ocean floor to stabilize the bridge, engineers cannot support the spans needed to cross thousands of kilometers of ocean.

What is the problem regarding pontoon bridges on the open ocean?
Pontoon bridges on the open ocean would fail because the environment is far too stormy and full of massive waves. Current structural materials cannot withstand such intense continuous dynamic stresses, causing a floating pontoon bridge to shake itself to pieces under extreme ocean wave action.

What is the problem regarding salt water corrosion on structural materials?
Salt water corrosion on structural materials turns maintenance into an absolute nightmare. Continuous exposure to salt water and salty ocean air rapidly degrades concrete and steel structural components, requiring constant, impossibly expensive repairs in severe maritime weather conditions.

What is the problem regarding extreme water pressure at the ocean floor?
Extreme water pressure at the ocean floor presents an immense structural hazard for a subsea tunnel because the massive weight of all that water exerts forces ten thousand times greater than the pressure felt at the bottom of a deep swimming pool.

What is the problem regarding structural leaks in a deep ocean tunnel?
Structural leaks in a deep ocean tunnel would cause immediate catastrophic failure because at such extreme water pressure, even small leaks at prefabricated tunnel section joins would penetrate materials like a cutting laser, causing the walls to crumble and drowning everyone inside.

What is the problem regarding tunnel ventilation over thousands of kilometers?
Tunnel ventilation over thousands of kilometers represents a monumental challenge because thousands of kilometers of tunnel would contain enormous volumes of dead, uncirculated air. Massively powerful fans and circulation systems would be required to keep fresh air moving constantly so drivers would not suffocate.

What is the problem regarding tectonic movement along the Mid Atlantic Ridge?
Tectonic movement along the Mid Atlantic Ridge creates severe geological instability because the Atlantic Ocean floor pulls itself apart at a rate of two point five centimeters every year. Any transoceanic tunnel crossing this ridge would have to withstand active volcanoes, underwater earthquakes, and continuous continental drift.

What is the problem regarding driver fatigue and emergency response times?
Driver fatigue and emergency response times pose severe safety risks for travelers. A driver would face many continuous hours of exhausting driving far beyond standard fuel ranges, and if a vehicle broke down or an emergency occurred in the middle of the tunnel, emergency personnel would take hours to reach the scene.

What is the problem regarding international jurisdiction and infrastructure maintenance?
International jurisdiction and infrastructure maintenance raise unresolved legal and political questions. Because the crossing would lie largely in international waters outside any single country, no specific nation or municipality would have responsibility for maintaining utilities, ensuring security, or repairing infrastructure.

What is the problem regarding economic viability and financial investment?
Economic viability and financial investment make the project extremely impractical today because construction costs would be astronomically high while practical benefits remain minimal, offering no realistic way for investors or governments to receive a return on their investment.

What is the problem regarding technological feasibility now and in the future?
Technological feasibility now and in the future suggests that while a transoceanic bridge or tunnel might be technically possible with present technology if politicians and scientists become completely determined, much like nineteenth century views on space travel, it remains highly unlikely for now, although future technological developments over coming decades could make such a crossing significantly more feasible.

Can you explain the primary reasons why a program might crash?
The primary reasons why a program might crash stem from common errors where software encounters a problem it cannot resolve.

Can you explain division by zero in programming?
Division by zero in programming occurs when code tells the computer to divide a number by zero. You may remember from kindergarten math that you cannot divide a number by zero because the result is undefined. If a program tells the computer to divide something by zero, the computer will tell the program that it is doing something wrong. If the program cannot handle that situation, it may crash.

Can you explain an access violation error?
An access violation error occurs because a program is only allowed to access certain parts of memory. Other parts are off limits. If a program tries to access part of memory that is off limits, the computer will tell the program that it is doing something wrong. If the program cannot handle that situation, it may crash.

Can you explain a deadlock situation in a program?
A deadlock situation in a program can be understood with an example. Suppose you have the red block and Billy has the blue block. You tell Billy you will give him your red block after he gives you his blue block. Billy tells you he will give you his blue block after you give him your red block. Both of you sit there forever waiting, and you never get anything done. When it happens inside a program, the program freezes up and there is nothing you can do except kill it and start it again.

Can you explain an unhandled exception in software?
An unhandled exception in software relates to error checking. Sometimes a program has a special sort of error checking built into it. When an error is detected, part of the program throws an exception, and another part is supposed to catch the exception and deal with it. If an exception gets thrown and is not caught by any part of the program, a dialog pops up letting you know a problem was not dealt with properly, and the program terminates.

Can you explain why bugs exist in programs?
Why bugs exist in programs comes down to code errors. All crash situations are caused by bugs in the program. Bugs are parts of code that are not written correctly or fail to account for every possible outcome. Some programs have more bugs because developers were in a rush, did not test properly, or because the program is so complicated that dealing with every possible situation is difficult.

Can you explain the peanut butter sandwich recipe analogy?
The peanut butter sandwich recipe analogy helps us think of a program as a way to do things. A common example is making a peanut butter and jelly sandwich. Your first program might read: get bread, get peanut butter, get jelly, get knife, put peanut butter on one slice, put jelly on other slice, put bread together, serve. If you run out of peanut butter, you are stuck halfway through without anywhere left to go, which is a crash.

Can you explain how a pizza restaurant illustrates program complexity?
How a pizza restaurant illustrates program complexity shows how larger systems function. A more complicated program describes how a pizza restaurant works. There are more ingredients, more ways to combine them, many workers coming and going simultaneously, and a bunch more things that can go wrong. Some problems can be fixed while others cannot. Unfixable things, or things people are too lazy to fix, are crashes.

What can you tell me about the camera's field of view?
The camera's field of view, abbreviated as FOV, is a concept familiar to big first person shooter gamers or camera users. If we consider what we can see as a cone starting at our eye and expanding out, then FOV is the angle between the two boundary lines. In shooter games FOV is often expanded by pros to gain an advantage, since it lets you see more of your surroundings.

What can you tell me about an example of altering a game's field of view?
An example of altering a game's field of view can be shown by comparing an expanded FOV of 65 degrees to the default of 45 degrees. With the larger FOV you can see more on the left and right. But you will also notice that two trailer objects look like they are farther away even though the player is standing in the same place. That is because as you increase the FOV you also change how light from distant objects converges on your 2D surface. A larger FOV means objects decrease in size faster as they get farther away, while decreasing FOV increases the apparent size of far away objects since they converge on a larger portion of the view area.

What can you tell me about the specific camera on the DSCOVR spacecraft?
The specific camera on the DSCOVR spacecraft used to take these pictures has a FOV of just 0.61 degrees. It is very effective at collecting light from far away objects because it is focused on a very small cone. It also means that the distance between the Earth and the Moon does not have the same effect on relative size as it does with a regular camera or human eyes.

What can you tell me about the hand and monitor perspective experiment?
The hand and monitor perspective experiment involves holding your hand in front of your face, where it is about as big as your monitor. Keep your hand in the same spot and move your head backwards. Your hand now appears smaller than the monitor. At a certain distance, your hand and the monitor get smaller together at the same rate. This is because the distance between you and those two things becomes much greater than the distance between those two things. Angular diameter depends on distance and ratio of distances.

What can you tell me about the relative apparent sizes of the Earth and the Moon?
The relative apparent sizes of the Earth and the Moon depend on observer position. The first image is very close to the moon and far from the earth, so the moon seems big. The second image is very far from both the earth and the moon, so they appear like their actual relative sizes. The earth DOES appear smaller in the second image, but the moon got smaller a lot faster just like your hand.

What can you tell me about the technical design of space cameras?
The technical design of space cameras explains why DSCOVR had its camera zoomed in more. The EPIC camera on the spacecraft is specifically designed to observe Earth from a distance, whereas Apollo mission cameras were more general purpose.

What can you tell me about how focal length and sensor size affect camera images?
How focal length and sensor size affect camera images depends on optics. In a camera, lens focal length determines the physical size of the image formed on the sensor. Physical sensor size determines FOV, and pixel resolution determines pixel size. Analogue film has no pixels but has resolution limits from chemistry and the lens. A large image can be cropped, although the DSCOVR image is pretty much its full size.

Could you tell me about different kinds of radiation?
Different kinds of radiation include ordinary light, radio waves, X-rays, and specifically ionizing radiation, which is the dangerous kind that nuclear bombs and power plants are based on.

Could you tell me about what an atom is?
What an atom is can be described as the fundamental building block of everything in the world, made up of protons, neutrons, and electrons, where different numbers or combinations result in different atoms.

Could you tell me about how unstable atoms behave?
How unstable atoms behave involves seeking stability by offloading protons, neutrons, and electrons over time very quickly, acting like tiny little bullets that strike other atoms at the atomic level with enough force to send their protons and neutrons scattering like a pool ball hitting a big group of pool balls.

Could you tell me about the process of radioactivity?
The process of radioactivity happens when certain elements are unstable, causing them to release particles and energy to increase stability because there are too many particles in the atom for it to be stable.

Could you tell me about the crowded elevator analogy?
The crowded elevator analogy compares an atom to a crowded elevator where so many people make everyone uncomfortable that some people leave the group instead of sticking together all the way to the top, until enough leave for it to become comfortable again.

Could you tell me about how lead is formed?
How lead is formed happens when uranium releases enough particles to make itself stable or comfortable enough for the particles to stay together without losing anyone.

Could you tell me about gamma rays and radiation?
Gamma rays and radiation relate to how radiation includes different types of light ranging from radio waves to X-rays, so when radioactive atoms fall apart and energetic bits fly off, gamma rays are a form of light and therefore count as radiation.

Could you tell me about historical confusion over radiation?
Historical confusion over radiation occurred because when scientists first discovered radioactivity, they did not fully understand the different kinds of light, leading to confusion over what was radiation and what was radioactivity, which is why some people still use radiation when they mean radioactivity.

Could you tell me about the summary of these definitions?
The summary of these definitions is that radiation is different kinds of light, radioactivity consists of bits that fly off of radioactive atoms, and gamma rays are both.
style_catechism.coling::3dd39352-d471-4ab9-bd50-b7345fc1:
Can you tell me about the terms wealth tax and capital tax?
The terms wealth tax and capital tax describe taxes not based on income earned in a year, but on some measure of how much you own.

Can you tell me about international examples of wealth taxes?
International examples of wealth taxes include Italy taxing foreign land, Canada taxing corporate amounts until five to ten years ago depending on the province, and Switzerland taxing wealth above a certain level.

Can you tell me about the United States estate tax?
The United States estate tax is one form of wealth tax that exists in the US, taxing wealth a person owns when they die. The threshold has been volatile over the last twenty years, but generally sits in the multi-millions around five million dollars.

Can you tell me about the future impact of a new wealth tax?
The future impact of a new wealth tax should not cause shock at the initial sticker price, because theoretically a wealth tax could replace some current income tax regime without creating an increased tax burden on people. If you owe ten thousand dollars in income tax this year, but a two thousand dollar capital tax is instituted next year, you remain in the same position if income tax is reduced to eight thousand dollars.

Can you tell me about whether wealth taxes are effective?
Whether wealth taxes are effective or preferable is really a question of economics, not personal finance, so I will not belabor that point.

Can you tell me about taxes on saved money and investment earnings?
Taxes on saved money and investment earnings apply if saved money earns interest, dividends, or condo rent, as those earnings are typically taxed alongside wage income, meaning any wealth tax would be in addition to income tax on investment earnings.

Can you provide information regarding whether you can lose money on both options on the same day?
Whether you can lose money on both options on the same day is unlikely, although both could be exercised and assigned on the same day.

Can you provide information regarding the processing time for option assignments?
The processing time for option assignments occurs after markets close each day, unlike immediate exercises, as detailed at http://www.888options.com/help/faq/assignment.jsp, so both assignments arrive simultaneously that night.

Can you provide information regarding your resulting stock ownership and options status?
Your resulting stock ownership and options status leaves you owning no stock, because someone puts stock to you and it gets called away, and holding no remaining options.

Can you provide information regarding the cash movement resulting from both exercises?
The cash movement resulting from both exercises includes incoming cash of $1500 selling stock to the call exerciser and outgoing cash of $1300 buying stock from the put exerciser, leaving $200 more cash in your account by morning.

Can you provide information regarding the basic nature of this options position?
The basic nature of this options position is an agreement to buy at 13 and sell at 15 at someone else's option.

Can you provide information regarding how a trader loses money on this position?
How a trader loses money on this position occurs if one option is exercised while the other is not, such as when stock drops below 13 or rises above 15.

Can you provide information regarding how a trader makes money on this position?
How a trader makes money on this position happens if neither option is exercised, keeping the sold premium, or if both are exercised, keeping the gap between strike prices plus premium.

Can you provide information regarding the likelihood of having both options exercised on the same day?
The likelihood of having both options exercised on the same day is rare because early exercise is rare, occurring when options are deep in the money, but it is most likely near expiration with minimal time value if the stock moves quickly so both are in the money during the day.

Can you explain the first step to take regarding credit card terms?
The first step to take regarding credit card terms is to look at your terms and conditions or ask your bank directly how they will apply your payments.

Can you explain how United States banks handle payment allocation?
How United States banks handle payment allocation involves applying the minimum payment to the lower rate balance, and applying any rest above the minimum to the higher rate balance.

Can you explain how payment rules vary in other countries?
How payment rules vary in other countries depends on law and custom, so you should never assume payments pay off the higher balance or apply proportionally without asking.

Can you explain the example scenario with two different interest rates?
The example scenario with two different interest rates involves owing $6000 total, where $5000 is at a 13.5% purchase rate and $1000 is at a 22% cash advance rate.

Can you explain how a proportional payment reduces balances?
How a proportional payment reduces balances means a payment of $600 will reduce the purchase balance by $500 and your cash advance balance by $100.

Can you explain how to calculate the weighted average interest rate?
How to calculate the weighted average interest rate is by summing the product of the APR times balance, calculating (.135 times 5000 plus .225 times 1000) divided by 6000 equals 15%.

Can you explain why a weighted average can be misleading over time?
Why a weighted average can be misleading over time is because if your bank pays the lower rate balance first, your average APR will rise over time as the purchase balance shrinks.

Can you explain when a weighted average is suitable for rough calculations?
When a weighted average is suitable for rough calculations is when rules do not 100% pay down the lower rate balance, making it a simple option when exact precision is not critical.

Can you explain how online calculators can treat balances as separate loans?
How online calculators can treat balances as separate loans allows you to allocate funds differently to two cards, showing how long it takes to pay off the higher balance.

Can you explain the main limitation of using online balance calculators?
The main limitation of using online balance calculators is that calculations probably will not match perfectly, meaning you must live with a small error or calculate the math by hand.

Can you provide the advice regarding planning your finances around your credit score?
Planning your finances around your credit score is something you must avoid; do not plan your finances around it or even think about your credit score at all.

Can you provide the advice regarding managing a personal budget?
Managing a personal budget means planning a budget and sticking to it, including short and long term savings, paying your bills on time, and using credit responsibly so your credit rating takes care of itself instead of trying to plan around raising it.

Can you provide the advice regarding zero percent financing?
Zero percent financing should only ever be used when you have enough money saved up to buy the item outright, and even then only if your budget will still balance with the added cost of repaying the loan.

Can you provide the advice regarding personal rules for taking loans?
Personal rules for taking loans vary, including avoiding such loans, and you should develop a rule that works for you, though never make a rule to do whatever optimizes your credit score because you shouldn't plan finances around it.

Can you provide the advice regarding introductory teaser rates?
Introductory teaser rates should not tempt you into making purchases you wouldn't otherwise make, since you are not really getting free money but just shifting around the time frame for payment within a limited window.

Can you provide the advice regarding reading the fine print in credit agreements?
Reading the fine print in credit agreements is essential because they can be filled with gotchas, such as incurring interest charges retroactively to the purchase date if you don't clear the balance by the end of the introductory rate period, so know your terms cold.

Can you provide the advice regarding patience for beginners in finance?
Patience for beginners in finance can be the most effective tool in your personal finance arsenal as you get started, so best of luck, remember that Rome wasn't built in a day, and do not plan your finances around your credit score.

What should one know about the assumption that companies listed on the OTC are not serious?
The assumption that companies listed on the OTC are not serious is far from the truth. Many companies start on the OTC market simply because they do not meet the listing requirements to be listed on major stock exchanges like the NASDAQ or NYSE, which only want the best companies to trade on their exchanges.

What should one know about the listing requirements for the NASDAQ exchange?
The listing requirements for the NASDAQ exchange include three sets of requirements. A company must meet at least one of these three requirement sets, as well as the main rules for all companies trading on that exchange.

What should one know about the regulatory requirements for the OTC market?
The regulatory requirements for the OTC market do exist. While there are no minimum levels of revenue, profits, or assets required to get listed on the OTC, there are requirements for audited financial statements and ongoing filing and reporting to the SEC and NASD.

What should one know about the different tiers of the OTC market?
The different tiers of the OTC market include the OTCQX, the OTCCB, and the OTC Pink, each with their own set of requirements. For more information about what it takes to be listed on OTC look here: http://www.otcmarkets.com/learn/otc-trading

What should one know about the financial investment to list on the OTC market?
The financial investment to list on the OTC market shows a company is making the decision to go public. Currently, the fees to get listed on the OTC range from $30,000 to $150,000 depending on the firm and services offered, which is certainly serious money.

What should one know about the requirements of getting listed on the TSX market?
The requirements of getting listed on the TSX market seem a lot more relaxed than those of the major U.S. markets, consisting of an application, records submission, and a decision made by a TSX committee. More information about the TSX is here: http://apps.tmx.com/en/listings/listing_with_us/process/index.html

What should one know about the reason OTC markets have a bad reputation?
The reason OTC markets have a bad reputation comes from "Get Rich on Penny Stock" companies pumping up OTC stocks so people buy without doing due diligence or reading the prospectus, then blaming the OTC stock when losing money on ill-informed decisions.

What should one know about the best method for making an investment decision?
The best method for making an investment decision should not be based on how many exchanges a company is listed on, but rather based on the research you do into the company.

Schools offering online or video conferencing classes improve student learning by giving students flexible ways to attend their courses. Starting in 2009, schools began providing this type of remote education program to the community so that students could participate in classes from home.

Can you explain how families living in the local area initially viewed this remote program?
Families living in the local area initially viewed this remote program with skepticism, as most local families thought this new educational program was useless when it first started.

Can you explain how families living at a far distance viewed the remote learning program?
Families living at a far distance viewed the remote learning program as a brilliant idea because it meant their children would not have to spend long terms of time traveling every single day to reach school.

Can you explain how the remote learning program at Generic_School began on September 2, 2009?
The remote learning program at Generic_School began on September 2, 2009, with around ninety-two students involved, all of whom liked the program during their initial year.

Can you explain how student enrollment changed during the second year of online classes?
Student enrollment changed during the second year of online classes when only seventy percent of the original group, which equaled sixty-five students, joined the online program.

Can you explain how students described their experiences and feelings during the second year?
Students described their experiences and feelings during the second year by commenting that it was nice to stay home and take classes online without worrying about being late, but expressing that as students they would love to share thoughts and ideas with peers.

Can you explain how student participation dropped sharply starting in the third year?
Student participation dropped sharply starting in the third year, around 2011, when enrollment decreased to ten percent, meaning only about twenty students joined the online program because being home all day felt boring without peer engagement or active movement.

Can you explain how new course options can help get students interested in the program again?
New course options can help get students interested in the program again by allowing students to choose before joining a class whether they want to go out and do projects with classmates, chat to gather information, and select meeting days.

Can you explain how alternative communication methods support students who prefer remote interaction?
Alternative communication methods support students who prefer remote interaction by providing video chat or voice chat options for those who do not wish to meet in person.

Can you explain how periodic campus visits can increase overall student involvement?
Periodic campus visits can increase overall student involvement by giving students the option to visit the physical school once a week or once a month, attracting more participants.

Local parents in 2009 raised concerns about physical school attendance by telling the principal that having an open online program would result in fewer students attending school, causing their long-standing attendance goals to fail.

Can you explain how the principal of Generic_School resolved the disagreement with local parents?
The principal of Generic_School resolved the disagreement with local parents by holding many reunions over the course of a month to clarify that while in-person attendance is preferred, some students cannot attend, making the program a beneficial opportunity; after a month, most parents accepted the goal.

Can you explain how families from far distances showed appreciation and support for the school?

style_catechism.coling::c0381ae0-3b9c-40a4-bc53-f4a76564:
Could you clarify the primary scope of this paper?
The primary scope of this paper is an extension of the Lenc&Vedaldi15 paper, showing CNN representations at FC7 layer are to a certain extent equivariant to various classes of transformations, and that training with a certain group of transformation makes the representations more equivalent.

Could you clarify the general evaluation and main message of this paper?
The general evaluation and main message of this paper reflects a large amount of experiments, training over thirty networks with different forms of jitter, which is quite impressive. However, it is rather difficult to find a main message. Yes, authors measured properties on a different layer than Lenc&Vedaldi15, but it is hard to find novel insights other than the known fact that jitter helps to achieve invariance, and the paper does not seem to solve the advertised task really well.

Could you clarify the first major issue regarding representation distances?
The first major issue regarding representation distances is that the selection of only FC7 is a bit controversial, as it is followed only by a single classification layer, FC8, to the common output class likelihoods. Because FC8 is just a linear projection, what the equivalence map does is just to re-project FC8 weights of the attached network to the weights of the original network. Probably performing similar experiments on more layers may be more useful, as networks are already trained.

Could you clarify the second major issue concerning missing test set classification error?
The second major issue concerning missing test set classification error is that the experiment with representation distance is missing what the classification error is on the testing dataset. This would answer whether the representations are actually compatible up to a linear transformation at all.

Could you clarify the third major issue regarding the K-NN experiment?
The third major issue regarding the K-NN experiment is that it is not clear whether this is measured per each test set example after training the equivalence map. More clear would be to show that networks trained on a similar group of jitter transformations are more compatible on the target task.

Could you clarify the fourth major issue concerning inconsistent equivariance improvements?
The fourth major issue concerning inconsistent equivariance improvements is that the proposed method does not seem to improve equivariance consistently on all tasks. Especially with lambda_1 and lambda_2 having such small values, the loss is basically equal to simple data jitter as it just adds up the loss of the original and transformed image. Maybe the issue lies in the selection of the FC7 layer.

Could you clarify the overall recommendation for this manuscript?
The overall recommendation for this manuscript is that while it shows some interesting results on FC7 equivariance, it does not draw many interesting new observations out of these experiments. Due to issues with equivalence experiments and finetuning of equivariance, acceptance is not recommended. However, refining experiments on trained networks and restructuring into a more investigative work may lead to an interesting contribution to the field.

Could you clarify the minor issues identified throughout the text?
The minor issues identified throughout the text include unverified equivariance mapping criteria, missing degree units on pages one and five, optimizing loss over M_g rather than M_g itself on page three, misnaming activation halving as dropout on page four, unconfirmed AlexNet architecture for RVL-CDIP, and turning diagonal matrix elements to white in Figures 3a and 3b when identical representation distance must equal zero to verify experiment correctness.
style_catechism.coling::07106895-c293-4117-be28-f7598533:
What is the comment regarding the appreciation and novelty of this paper?
The appreciation and novelty of this paper starts with thank you for an interesting read. I personally like the information bottleneck principle and am happy to see its application to deep neural networks. To my knowledge, this is the first paper that applies IB to train deep networks (the original papers only presented the concept), but see below for independent work claim.

What is the comment regarding the derivations and experimental results?
The derivations and experimental results are clear. The derivation of the variational lowerbound is very clear, even for those who are not very familiar with variational inference. Also the explanation of the IB principle is clear. Experimental results seem to be very promising.

What is the comment regarding the model presentation?
The model presentation is confusing. In variational inference or information maximisation, p usually denotes the model and q represents the inference engine. This means the choice of inference method is independent to the modelling procedure. However the presented VIB assumed p(x,y) as the underlying data distribution (approximated by the empirical distribution), making the model actually q(y|z)p(z|x).

What is the comment regarding the predictive distribution?
The predictive distribution was presented as p(y|x) in page 8, paragraph 2 of section 4.2.3. Predictive in what sense? I guess you meant p(y|x) = \int q(y|z) p(z|x) dz in this case, but this makes the two definitions contradict to each other!

What is the comment regarding the connection to variational auto-encoders?
The connection to variational auto-encoders includes warm-up training by tuning beta. However, even when the loss function formula is the same to the variational lowerbound in VAE (beta = 1), the underlying model is different! For example, r(z) in VIB is the variational approximation to p(z) (not a component in the model), while in VAE it is the prior distribution defined in modelling. Similarly p(z|x) in VIB is included in the model, while in VAE that is the approximate posterior.

What is the comment regarding the overall summary and revision recommendations?
The overall summary and revision recommendations state that I think the presentation for the modelling procedure is unclear. I hope these points would be made clearer in revision since the current presentation makes me uncomfortable as a Bayesian person. In the VAE part, it is better to clearly mention the difference between VIB and VAE, and provide some intuitions if the VIB interpretation is preferred.

What is the comment regarding potential typos?
Potential typos include Eq. 9-11: did you mean q(y|z) instead of q(z|y)? Also Fig 2 "as beta becomes smaller": did you mean "larger"?

What is the comment regarding the claim for independent work?
The claim for independent work notes that the authors claimed the manuscript presented independent work to Chalk et al. 2016 (online since May 2016). Deep learning research is very competitive so many people publish the same idea at the same time. I trust this claim and commend the authors' honesty, but if not true, I would not recommend acceptance.
style_catechism.coling::745b25d5-34c6-4c43-a690-6414f205:
What can be said regarding the machine translation training data selection approach?
The machine translation training data selection approach described in the paper scores and ranks general-domain sentences using a convolutional neural network classifier. Comparison to prior work using continuous or n-gram based language models is well done, though it is unclear if the paper compared against bilingual data selection like the sum of difference of cross-entropies.

What can be said regarding the motivation to use a convolutional neural network instead of a recurrent neural network?
The motivation to use a convolutional neural network instead of a recurrent neural network was first unclear, but it is a strength of the paper to argue that certain sections of a text are more important than others. However, the paper does not experimentally show whether a bag-of-words or sequence representation is more important and why.

What can be said regarding the textual description of the convolutional neural network?
The textual description of the convolutional neural network is clear and detailed, though a picture of the layers showing how inputs are combined would be worth a thousand words.

What can be said regarding the overall writing quality and citation formatting?
The overall writing quality and citation formatting are generally good, but some parentheses for citations are unnecessary, such as line 385.

What can be said regarding the experimental validation data and hyperparameter settings?
The experimental validation data and hyperparameter settings raise concerns regarding determining the number of selected in-domain sentences on line 443 based on a separate validation set. It is unclear what validation data is used, what hyperparameters are chosen on, and how sensitive models are to this.

What can be said regarding the comparisons presented in Table 2?
The comparisons presented in Table 2 should compare scores with the same number of sentences selected, where the approach still appears to outperform baselines as shown in Figure 1.

What can be said regarding additional experiments with larger in-domain datasets?
Additional experiments with larger in-domain datasets would be interesting to compare against baselines when more in-domain data is available, not just the development set.

What can be said regarding example sentences in section 5.4?
Example sentences in section 5.4 could be featured in results or discussion to support the claims made by showing sentences selected by different methods.

What can be said regarding comparisons against Axelrod 2015?
Comparisons against Axelrod 2015 could be another baseline, replacing words with POS tags to reduce LM data sparsity to see whether word2vec embeddings provide an advantage.

What can be said regarding the relationship to Lewis-Moore data selection?
The relationship to Lewis-Moore data selection is notable because using the sum of source and target classification scores is very similar to Lewis-Moore LM data selection. A reference around line 435 is reasonable, and one wonders if weights could be learned for both scores by extending the CNN model to a bilingual setting.
style_catechism.coling::a0b0f9d5-62dc-4996-9de4-5e5f9b3b:
What can be said regarding the introduction of the paper?
The introduction of the paper outlines Edward, a probabilistic programming language built over TensorFlow and Python that supports a broad range of contemporary methods in probabilistic machine learning.

What can be said regarding the quality of the library?
The quality of the library is evident in its impressive collection of modern probabilistic inference methods provided in an easily usable form, alongside a brief review of techniques from a representation learning perspective and two experiments.

What can be said regarding the variational inference experiment?
The variational inference experiment would be more valuable if there were a clear link to complete code required to reproduce the presented results.

What can be said regarding the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo experiment?
The Hamiltonian Monte Carlo experiment looks acceptable overall, except that characterising Stan as a hand-optimised implementation seems unfair since the code is clearly not hand-optimised for this specific model and hardware configuration.

What can be said regarding the performance claims and comparison?
The performance claims and comparison should avoid sensationalist assertions; instead, the authors should compare head-to-head against Stan on a single core and separately report extra speedups gained from parallelisation and GPU execution to help readers estimate performance for other hardware configurations.

What can be said regarding the clarity of the paper?
The clarity of the paper is generally good as it is easy to read, but the code examples are difficult because it is sometimes unclear what is missing, so providing a clearly linked machine-readable companion like a Jupyter notebook, text, or HTML file with complete runnable code would be very helpful.

What can be said regarding the originality of the work?
The originality of the work is supported by Edward being a unique collection of inference methods, though a threat to novelty comes from a previous paper by the same group (Tran et al., 2016a), and it remains unclear if that paper has been published or submitted anywhere.

What can be said regarding the significance of Edward?
The significance of Edward seems very likely to be profound, as it will likely have a major impact on the fields of Bayesian machine learning and deep learning.

What can be said regarding the language categorization in Section 2?
The language categorization in Section 2 draws a clear distinction between specialised languages like Stan and Turing-complete languages such as Edward, which seems unfair because Stan is also Turing complete, and furthermore, no proof is provided to support the Turing-completeness of Edward.

What is the review feedback regarding the general novelty of this submission?

What is the review feedback regarding perplexity for unknown words in Section 4.2?
