What is the review feedback regarding vocabulary reporting in Section 4.4 and Table 4?
Vocabulary reporting in Section 4.4 and Table 4 should explicitly include the full training vocabulary size.

What is the review feedback regarding the grammar error on page 2?
The grammar error on page 2 requires changing "three different input layer" to "three different input layers".

What is the review feedback regarding Figure 1 font size?
Figure 1 font size must be increased because fonts within the figure are way too small.

What is the review feedback regarding the notation error on page 3?
The notation error on page 3 below Figure 1 should change "that we will note WE" to "that we will denote WE".

What is the review feedback regarding the phrasing error in Section 2.3?
The phrasing error in Section 2.3 should change "the parameters estimation" to "the parameter estimation".

What is the review feedback regarding article omission on page 5?
Article omission on page 5 paragraph 1 requires changing "in factored way" to "in a factored way".

What is the review feedback regarding article choices on page 5?
Article choices on page 5 paragraph 2 require changing "a n-best list, a nk-best list" to "an n-best list, an nk-best list".

What is the review feedback regarding the last sentence of Section 4.2?
The last sentence of Section 4.2 starting "Despite adaptive gradient," is incomplete, lacking a verb and an article.
style_catechism.coling::d8e4451f-f606-413a-a2c5-5f2b5e9c:
What is the reviewer's critique regarding the extreme length of this seventeen page submission?
The extreme length of this seventeen page submission is a major initial concern because the paper spans seventeen full pages without supplementary material. While ICLR lacks an official page limit, authors should put themselves in the reviewer's shoes and avoid taking undue advantage of this rule. Adding one or two pages beyond the conventional eight-page limit is acceptable, but more than doubling the standard page count is quite unfair.

What is the reviewer's critique regarding the core proposal and experimental summary of the paper?
The core proposal and experimental summary of the paper centered on introducing a new artificial dataset for sequence learning alongside a training regimen. The dataset is called artificial because it was generated from the original MNIST dataset, which is a small dataset of real handwritten digits. The authors propose training recurrent networks using a schedule over sequence length, termed incremental learning. Experiments show that their proposed schedule outperforms having no schedule on this dataset and beats a few intuitive schedules. The authors verify this through ablation studies over the model on the proposed dataset.

What is the reviewer's critique regarding the novelty of the proposed incremental learning schedule?
The novelty of the proposed incremental learning schedule is lacking, as I found nothing novel in this paper. The proposed incremental learning schedule is nothing new and represents a natural thing to try when learning sequences. Similar ideas have already been tried by several authors, including Bengio in 2015 and Ranzato in 2015. The only new piece of work is the set of ablation studies conducted to tease out and verify that the performance improvement is indeed due to the curriculum used.

What is the reviewer's critique regarding the limited evaluation on a single synthetic dataset?
The limited evaluation on a single synthetic dataset raises issues because the authors only test their hypothesis on a single artificial dataset they proposed. Why not use a real sequential dataset, such as language modeling? Does the technique not work in that scenario? For language modeling where vocabulary size is huge, performance gains will likely be nowhere close to the seventy-four percent reported in the paper.

What is the reviewer's critique regarding the overall value of introducing this artificial dataset?
The overall value of introducing this artificial dataset is unconvincing to me. Many real-world sequential datasets are already available in text, speech, finance, and other areas, so what this dataset brings to the table is not clear. While having another dataset is not bad, I felt this dataset was created solely to make the proposed ideas work. It would have been better had the authors shown experiments on other datasets.

What is the reviewer's critique regarding the inclusion of completely unrelated experimental sections?
The inclusion of completely unrelated experimental sections makes the paper way too long. A significant part of the length is due to experiments completely unrelated to the main message. For instance, the experiment in Section 6.2 is completely unrelated to the story of the paper. The same is true with the transfer learning experiments of Section 6.4.
style_catechism.coling::60e5cc06-240c-4ed3-80bd-353d0ba8:
Can you provide details about the financial limitation of solar power? The financial limitation of solar power is that while solar power is a miracle of modern science, it is still more expensive than using other forms of power. If it was not for the cost, it would be a much better idea, but that limitation goes for all forms of renewable energy.

Can you provide details about comparing solar panel installation to building power plants? Comparing solar panel installation to building power plants shows that installing solar is on par with or cheaper than building new plants like nuclear or coal on a large scale. However, you are probably not going to build your own power plant and don't have that expense, so look at panel cost versus average power output and do the math.

Can you provide details about government involvement in solar and nuclear energy? Government involvement in solar and nuclear energy includes subsidizing solar power purchases in California in a huge way. Furthermore, the government does not operate nuclear power plants; those are operated by private corporations and merely regulated by the government.

Can you provide details about the economic impact of shutting down nuclear power plants? The economic impact of shutting down nuclear power plants must take into account that the primary cost of a nuclear plant is construction and material disposal, not running the plant itself. Consequently, shutting down a working plant would waste money rather than save money.

Can you provide details about the operational advantages of solar power? The operational advantages of solar power include its point of use nature, meaning very little loss due to long distance transmission, practically zero emissions, completely silent operation, and providing the greatest benefit in summer daytimes when demand is highest.

Can you provide details about using solar energy for running air conditioning? Using solar energy for running air conditioning is possibly the best application of solar power. During summer when the sun is strong, air cooling demand is strong. Using sunlight captured by solar panels to cool buildings, while the rooftop panels simultaneously shade the building, creates a doubly beneficial outcome.

Can you provide details about the pure cost benefit analysis of electricity sources? The pure cost benefit analysis of electricity sources reveals that, despite all advantages, it remains cheaper to use coal or natural gas to provide electricity.
style_catechism.coling::ef4cca12-c45c-4b1b-9c67-8db766ad:
What can you tell me about the business opportunity available to a merchant living in seventeenth century Amsterdam?
The business opportunity available to a merchant living in seventeenth century Amsterdam revolves around a group of super rich ladies who love the spice known as cumin. Because cumin does not grow anywhere near Amsterdam, a merchant must travel to the Middle East or India to obtain it, making the spice outrageously expensive locally. In those distant lands, however, cumin grows like a weed and costs very little money. If a merchant can transport that cheap cumin back home, huge profits can be made.

What can you tell me about the immense risks and expenses involved in sending out a cargo ship?
The immense risks and expenses involved in sending out a cargo ship stem from needing to send a vessel on a journey lasting nine months. Purchasing or preparing a ship and paying a captain and crew nine months of wages is hugely expensive. Furthermore, the journey is extremely risky, because the boat could sink or the entire cargo of cumin could spoil during the voyage.

What can you tell me about the severe dangers of financing the voyage through a traditional bank loan?
The severe dangers of financing the voyage through a traditional bank loan arise because very few individuals are wealthy enough to pay for such a journey alone. Taking out a loan from a bank or moneylender involves a steep interest rate that could eat up nearly all the profits. If the boat sinks, the merchant faces complete bankruptcy, imprisonment in a debtors prison, or even harm from the moneylender.

What can you tell me about the strategy of dividing the financial costs among multiple investors?
The strategy of dividing the financial costs among multiple investors occurs when a merchant buys a one tenth share in the enterprise and finds nine friends to cover the remaining costs by purchasing their own shares. With this shared money, they pay for the boat and crew, send them off, and nine months later welcome back a hold full of valuable cumin. The resulting profits far exceed the initial costs and are shared equally among all ten participants.

What can you tell me about the outcome if a jointly funded ship ends up sinking?
The outcome if a jointly funded ship ends up sinking is much less devastating than if one person paid for everything. Although it is a major disappointment, each investor only paid one tenth of the total expense, which is a cost they can afford to lose. Because the risk is spread among ten people, nobody is forced into a debtors prison, and everyone takes a small financial hit instead of one person suffering total destruction.

What can you tell me about how the stock enterprise leaves every single person better off?
How the stock enterprise leaves every single person better off can be seen by examining everyone involved. The wealthy ladies get cheaper cumin, shipwrights earn money building a ship, the captain and crew obtain jobs and wages, the trader in India gains a new customer, and the merchant and his friends become very rich. Every single person benefits, which would not happen without the concept of buying and selling stocks.

What can you tell me about the fundamental advantages of running a stock market?
The fundamental advantages of running a stock market center on moving capital around from where it sits doing nothing to where it can be put to productive use, making everybody richer in the process. It also distributes financial risk among many people, meaning individuals do not have to live in constant fear of going completely broke.

What can you tell me about the modern critiques and enduring benefits of the stock market concept?
The modern critiques and enduring benefits of the stock market concept show that while the modern American stock market faces valid criticism for becoming an end unto itself rather than allocating capital productively, the underlying concept remains fantastic. Only hardcore communists would oppose a system responsible for enabling railroads, cars, computers, telephones, affordable food, medicine, and all the other modern things we value.
style_catechism.coling::108b67b9-1113-4b28-81da-e218ced4:
What should you know about business tax setup? Business tax setup depends on whether your business is a sole proprietorship, single member LLC, multi member LLC, an LLC with an S tax election, an S corporation, or a C corporation.

What should you know about a sole proprietorship? A sole proprietorship passes all profits and losses to you individually, leaving you personally liable. Pro tip: form an LLC or consult a business attorney.

What should you know about a single member LLC? A single member LLC passes profits and losses to you personally, but liability is limited to company assets. You also pay self employment tax.

What should you know about a multi member LLC? A multi member LLC splits profits and losses in proportion to each member ownership interest. You also pay self employment tax.

What should you know about an LLC with an S tax election? An LLC with an S tax election lets you pay a reasonable salary not subject to self employment tax. Remaining profits and losses pass through to shareholders by percentage interest. Tax on distributions depends on basis, which is complicated, so let your CPA worry about it.

What should you know about an S corporation? An S corporation follows the exact same tax treatment described above.

What should you know about a C corporation? A C corporation pays tax on profits at the corporate level, then dividends are taxed again. This double taxation makes C corporations not ideal for small business owners.

What should you know about a non profit seed faith mega church? A non profit seed faith mega church is an unethical trick to live lavishly tax free without hard work. Go on TV, convince followers to send money, and claim god will return ten times their faith seed.
style_catechism.coling::31049c2c-a6a8-44a9-acaa-b8e3b123:
What is the truth about online confrontation?
Online confrontation happens because people are anonymous and far outside the reach of those they disagree with, making them much more aggressive when there is no chance of being punched in the face.

What is the truth about physical intimidation?
Physical intimidation controls real world behavior. A person five feet tall and weighing ninety pounds soaking wet will not tell a six foot five guy weighing two hundred fifty pounds he is full of shit, but online nobody cares.

What is the truth about internet dehumanization?
Internet dehumanization occurs when the person you speak to is just words on a screen, making it much easier to be abusive, aggressive, or honest.

What is the truth about online harassment?
Online harassment makes it easy to watch a bad video and tell an anonymous username they are a talentless piece of shit. It is a different thing to walk up to Jenny, a fourteen year old girl making Minecraft videos to cope with her parents' divorce, look her in the eye, and say that to her.

What is the truth about vehicle isolation?
Vehicle isolation involves being inside a big locked metal box that is half suit of armor and half escape pod. You can lean on your horn and give the middle finger because you will never see that driver again.

What is the truth about road rage targets?
Road rage targets are treated like stupid cars rather than real people. Drivers curse out a Ford that cut them off, ignoring that it is driven by Jenny's mom who had a terrible day and is distracted because she cannot pay rent.
style_catechism.coling::564547e8-c996-4ee6-8beb-abfe8062:
Can you explain the basic premise of clap energy?
The basic premise of clap energy is that the overall energy of a clap remains unchanged, which means we must carefully examine where all of that collision energy is actually going.

Can you explain the energy destinations for a regular clap on earth?
The energy destinations for a regular clap on earth include the sound produced, the physical deformation of your hands, the heat generated, and several other minor factors that are probably constant in both scenarios and can be ignored.

Can you explain a simple mathematical model of a clap?
A simple mathematical model of a clap assumes two hands weighing five hundred grams each moving at two meters per second, which calculates to roughly four Joules of input energy using the equation energy equals mass times velocity squared.

Can you explain the small energy loss to hand deformation?
The small energy loss to hand deformation occurs because even though a clap would be considered an elastic collision, one would expect to see a tiny amount of damage to cells under a microscope.

Can you explain the primary consumer of energy in a clap?
The primary consumer of energy in a clap is going to be the heat given off by the colliding hands.

Can you explain the calculation of sound energy from a clap?
The calculation of sound energy from a clap relies on a clap lasting about twenty milliseconds and having a sound power similar to an alarm clock, yielding a rough wave integration of two times ten to the minus six Joules of sound energy.

Can you explain the percentage of energy converted to sound on earth?
The percentage of energy converted to sound on earth equals only zero point zero zero zero zero five percent of the four Joules of total energy released, with the remainder going into heat and hand deformation.

Can you explain how clap energy behaves in the vacuum of space?
How clap energy behaves in the vacuum of space involves zero percent of the energy going into sound, so that tiny amount simply becomes more heat, leaving the overall physical interaction essentially unchanged except you hear no sound.
style_catechism.coling::0303abd4-4ede-45e6-94d9-7e4d9969:
Could you provide information about worst-case global climate change projections?
Worst-case global climate change projections show that the ultimate outcome is certainly bad, with most of this change occurring near the poles and in the oceans.

Could you provide information about climate conditions during the Cretaceous period?
Climate conditions during the Cretaceous period represented the warmest period in geologic history over the last few hundred million years, occurring around 100 to 65 million years ago when carbon dioxide concentrations were around 1000 parts per million and global temperature was around 10 degrees Celsius higher than today.

Could you provide information about potential future emissions and warming trends?
Potential future emissions and warming trends that begin to approach Cretaceous levels are certainly not out of the question by the end of next century, though the likelihood of that specific scenario is debatable.

Could you provide information about geological features and weather during the Cretaceous era?
Geological features and weather during the Cretaceous era featured sea levels hundreds of meters higher than today, central North America submerged under a shallow inland sea, deciduous forests growing in polar regions, and dramatically increased severity and frequency of damaging weather events like hurricanes and typhoons.

Could you provide information about severe societal and geographic impacts of extreme warming?
Severe societal and geographic impacts of extreme warming mean most of the tropics would be uninhabitable or extremely unpleasant due to heat and humidity, large land portions would be submerged displacing hundreds of millions or billions of people, fresh water would grow scarce as glacier sources melt completely, and northern Canadian wilderness would have Mediterranean-esque climates.

Could you provide information about ocean changes and mass extinction consequences?
Ocean changes and mass extinction consequences involve huge changes in ocean salinity and pH causing mass extinction of ocean wildlife which is a major food source for humans, mass extinction of species unable to adapt or move quickly, disturbance of migratory species, and huge human migrations to temperate zones destroying environments supporting millions of species.
style_catechism.coling::8e0f7cff-07ca-48c6-b381-34b577d1:
What can you tell me about how babies form speech before using language?
How babies form speech before using language involves producing early babble. Basically, young infants play with generating vocal noises through open and closed mouth movements. These open and closed mouth movements are the easiest utterances for developmental babies to make as they explore sounds.

What can you tell me about the binary code of open and closed mouths?
The binary code of open and closed mouths can be understood with zero representing an open vowel sound, like aaaaaa. Meanwhile, the number one, or in our case a closed mouth, represents a closed consonant sound, such as m or p.

What can you tell me about producing the basic ma and pa sounds?
Producing the basic ma and pa sounds occurs when you try it yourself by closing your mouth as if making the beginning of an m or p word, then just opening your mouth and pushing through some air.

What can you tell me about interchangeable closed consonants in babbling?
Interchangeable closed consonants in babbling include sounds like B, D, and P, which are pretty much interchangeable. These produce variations such as baba, abba, papa, and dada. So, these basic building blocks of vocalisation represent the simplest form for the human mouth, which is why babies use them.

What can you tell me about pre-linguistic babies naming mother and father?
Pre-linguistic babies naming mother and father is an interesting topic because these infants have been the ones to give birth to language in the naming of parents. Why did we follow their lead? Maybe the simple naming of poo and wee in many languages follows a similar explanation.

What can you tell me about binary forms for grandparents in Hindi?
Binary forms for grandparents in Hindi also demonstrate these similar binary forms in many languages. These Hindi examples include daadaa for paternal grandfather, daadii for paternal grandmother, naanaa for maternal grandfather, and naanii for maternal grandmother.
style_catechism.coling::97ce3bac-5618-4fcb-8600-bcf08ed8:
What should you know regarding choosing between two similar wine bottles?
Choosing between two similar wine bottles is difficult unless you are very experienced, so to be blunt, you probably will not be able to look at two similar bottles and immediately figure out which one you will like better.

What should you know regarding finding out what wine types you like?
Finding out what wine types you like requires you to figure out what kind of wines you like in general by actually trying a few of those wines.

What should you know regarding the drawbacks of trying different wines?
The drawbacks of trying different wines include the reality that this can cost some money. Additionally, if you are actually five years old, then it is illegal to buy wine in the United States.

What should you know regarding how wines are generally divided?
How wines are generally divided depends on where the grapes were grown and the species of grape, which is called the wine's varietal.

What should you know regarding common red varietals?
Common red varietals include Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Syrah (sometimes called Shiraz), and Zinfandel.

What should you know regarding common white varietals?
Common white varietals include Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris (sometimes called Pinot Grigio), Riesling, and Gewurztraminer.

What should you know regarding what to do when you taste wines?
What to do when you taste wines is to pay attention to what you like about them.

What should you know regarding tannic taste in red wines?
Tannic taste in red wines refers to a distinctive taste in many red wines that makes your mouth feel dry, caused by molecules called tannins. If you like tannic wines, a tannic varietal, like Cabernet Sauvignon, might be good for you.

What should you know regarding noticeable traits in white wines?
Noticeable traits in white wines commonly include acidity, which is sourness, and sugar content, though you probably do not need an explanation of what qualifies as sour or sugary.

What should you know regarding oakiness in wine?
Oakiness in wine is another common trait to look for in red or white wine. If you detect a wood-like scent in the wine, that means that the wine has an oaky flavor.

What should you know regarding the idea of a universally great wine?
The idea of a universally great wine is a myth, as there is no such thing as a universally great wine. All that matters is which kind you like best, even if that means choosing to drink a $10 jug of wine over a $500 bottle of fancy Cabernet from Bordeaux.

What should you know regarding getting help when buying wine?
Getting help when buying wine involves asking the waiter, sommelier, or wine shop employee to help you out whenever you are in doubt. Usually, if you have a vague idea of what you want, they can help you find something you would like in your price range.
style_catechism.coling::ae050f0f-463e-4780-8638-108ef778:
What can be said about the main reasons Alexander won?
The main reasons Alexander won begin with the fact that Alexander was not outnumbered by as much as was first thought.

What can be said about the estimated size of Darius' army?
The estimated size of Darius' army is disputed, as modern historians find Arrian's count of six hundred thousand unlikely due to logistical difficulties fielding over one hundred thousand soldiers. Hans Delbrück estimates twenty-five thousand, though most scholars like Engels and Green estimate no more than one hundred thousand at Issus, including eleven thousand cavalry, ten thousand Immortals, and ten thousand Greek mercenaries, while Warry estimates one hundred eight thousand.

What can be said about the equipment of the Macedonian troops?
The equipment of the Macedonian troops was superior to regular Persian forces, being matched only by Persia's Greek mercenaries. Though outnumbered, much of Persia's force consisted of peltasts, leaving roughly equal numbers of melee infantry.

What can be said about the Companion cavalry?
The Companion cavalry were the best in the world at the time, so the Persian horse stood no chance against them.

What can be said about the hammer and anvil shock tactic?
The hammer and anvil shock tactic is the quintessential maneuver of warfare, where one force fixes a group while another slams into their rear to cause mass destruction and confusion, making it an extremely effective maneuver physically and psychologically.

What can be said about battle casualties and military discipline?
Battle casualties and military discipline are related because most casualties occur when one side runs away, proving that raw numbers do not equal discipline, which is the most essential thing an army can have.
style_catechism.coling::f249dac3-f3a2-4db9-9758-e18c9f8f:
Can you explain how the apartment residents in a town start searching for houses?
The apartment residents in a town all live in apartments, and some of them are looking to move to houses.

Can you explain how the local house builders respond to this demand?
The local house builders see this demand and start building houses.

Can you explain how high buyer demand affects housing prices?
High buyer demand can push prices higher as there is more competition for supply, which is the opposite of competition on the supply side where it brings prices down.

Can you explain how prices for these houses continue to climb?
Prices for these houses continue to climb as a bunch of people buy at high demand prices and overall demand remains high.

Can you explain how a drop in house demand eventually occurs?
A drop in house demand occurs once the price gets too high or most demand subsides from everyone wanting a house having one, dropping the purchasing cost.

Can you explain how homeowners who already purchased react to this shift?
Homeowners who already purchased now see themselves as losing money and want to move back into an apartment while getting rid of the house, which cranks up supply.

Can you explain how the precipitous drop on prices eventually stabilizes?
The precipitous drop on prices continues until prices reach a level where demand begins to stabilize at a new level.

Can you explain how a market bubble is defined?
A market bubble really comes down to a low supply, high demand market quickly changing to a high supply, low demand market.

Can you explain how both market conditions help themselves?
Both market conditions help themselves: high demand brings people in to invest and take advantage of price increases, while low demand gets people to try to push away from the market, making supply even higher.

style_catechism.coling::f4f3b137-0da5-4cc5-a8e0-08f5a284:
What can be explained about high-speed signal transmission in a wire?
High-speed signal transmission in a wire cannot be thought of as simple digital signals traveling in a cable. High-speed signal transmission in a wire must be understood as an analog signal process, because signals do not change instantly from one to zero and require time to travel.

What can be explained about signal propagation speed in a Cat 5 cable?
Signal propagation speed in a Cat 5 cable travels at 0.64 times the speed of light, which corresponds to 4.8 to 5.3 nanoseconds per meter. For 100Mbit ethernet, transmission runs at 100 million bits per second, which equals 100 bits in 1000 nanoseconds, or 1 bit in 10 nanoseconds.

What can be explained about multiple bits coexisting inside a cable?
Multiple bits coexisting inside a cable means that if an ethernet cable is longer than 2 meters, there is more than one bit in the cable. A cable can be 100 meters long, so there will be 50 bits inside the cable simultaneously, meaning the signal is obviously not the same across the entire cable length.

What can be explained about the practical bitrate inside a cable?
The practical bitrate inside a cable is higher in practice because of encoding.

What can be explained about ethernet signal image diagrams and eye patterns?
Ethernet signal image diagrams and eye patterns are shown at URL_1 and URL_0, displaying how different signals overlap. The system must determine if the signal is at the top, middle, or bottom where the black gaps reside.

What can be explained about signal noise and small eye openings?
Signal noise and small eye openings show that the signal is noisy and the eyes are small. The smaller the eyes, the harder it is to determine the signal state, and if they disappear, you cannot detect the signal.

What can be explained about cable physical properties and signal propagation factors?
Cable physical properties and signal propagation factors depend on the distance between wires, wire thickness, material properties, surrounding environmental interference, and cross-pair interference. Recognizing that noisy analog signals require predictable cable behaviors leads to setting standards.

What can be explained about twisted wire pairs and standard compliance?
Twisted wire pairs and standard compliance require wires to be twisted at specific relative rates to minimize interference. Having wires with known electrical parameters that work with hardware requires sticking to established standards.

What can be explained about high-speed data transmission using barbed wire?
High-speed data transmission using barbed wire can function if you know what you are doing, as shown in URL_2. High-speed data transmission using barbed wire requires the barbed wire pairs to be close and parallel while keeping adjacent pairs far apart. An article explains that barbed wire in this configuration has a similar signal effect as a Cat 5 cable, whereas non-parallel wires or closer pairs would fail.
style_catechism.coling::817b2dbf-699e-4bec-825a-2bbdf598:
What can you tell us about the primary role of an Intrusion Detection System? The primary role of an Intrusion Detection System is to serve as a key cybersecurity tool for network administrators by identifying malicious traffic and cyberattacks.

What can you tell us about the current limitation of machine learning based systems? The current limitation of machine learning based systems is that despite using deep learning algorithms to detect attacks faster, they lack robustness against previously unseen cyberattacks, particularly those targeting Internet of Things devices.

What can you tell us about the main goal of this research? The main goal of this research is to explore leveraging generative adversarial models to enhance the robustness of machine learning based detection systems.

What can you tell us about the proposed SIGMA method? The proposed SIGMA method leverages adversarial examples to strengthen intrusion detection systems against new types of attacks.

What can you tell us about the iterative process of SIGMA? The iterative process of SIGMA uses Generative Adversarial Networks and metaheuristics to generate adversarial examples iteratively, retraining a machine learning based system until detection rate convergence.

What can you tell us about the three phases in each improvement round? The three phases in each improvement round consist of a generative phase generating instances, an evaluation phase calculating the detection rate of newly generated attacks, and a training phase training the system with those attacks.

What can you tell us about the empirical evaluation and results of SIGMA? The empirical evaluation and results of SIGMA show that evaluating four standard machine learning classification algorithms with a combination of generative adversarial networks and a hybrid local search and genetic algorithm successfully generates adversarial attacks and improves detection performance up to one hundred percent in two rounds.
style_catechism.coling::0c653e8b-8157-47f3-bdaa-142023fb:
Question: What is known about the binary value principle?
Answer: The binary value principle is a simple subset-sum instance expressing that a natural number written in binary cannot be negative, relating to central problems in proof and algebraic complexity.

Question: What is known about the Ideal Proof System?
Answer: The Ideal Proof System is the strong algebraic proof system introduced by Grochow and Pitassi.

Question: What is known about conditional lower bounds from the Shub-Smale hypothesis?
Answer: Conditional lower bounds from the Shub-Smale hypothesis show that the hypothesis implies a superpolynomial lower bound on the size of Ideal Proof System refutations of the binary value principle over the rationals, defined as the unsatisfiable linear equation summing two to the power of i minus one times x sub i to negative one, for boolean variables.

Question: What is known about conditional lower bounds from the tau-conjecture?
Answer: Conditional lower bounds from the tau-conjecture show that the related tau-conjecture implies a superpolynomial lower bound on the size of Ideal Proof System refutations of a variant of the binary value principle over the ring of rational functions.

Question: What is known about prior conditional lower bounds for these proof systems?
Answer: Prior conditional lower bounds for these proof systems were not known for the Ideal Proof System or for propositional systems such as Frege.

Question: What is known about the connection to boolean formulas?
Answer: The connection to boolean formulas is that the binary value principle is not a direct translation of a boolean formula, so lower bounds on this principle do not necessarily entail lower bounds for Frege or its subsystems.

Question: What is known about the paradigm of Forbes et al.?
Answer: The paradigm of Forbes et al. obtained lower bounds against subsystems of the Ideal Proof System using restricted algebraic circuit lower bounds, which this work extends to full-fledged Ideal Proof System proofs.

Question: What is known about semi-algebraic versus algebraic reasoning?
Answer: Semi-algebraic versus algebraic reasoning is captured by the binary value principle, showing that admitting short refutations of this principle is necessary for any algebraic proof system to simulate any known semi-algebraic proof system, and for sufficiently strong systems it is also sufficient.

Question: What is known about the Cone Proof System?
Answer: The Cone Proof System is a very strong proof system introduced as a semi-algebraic analogue of the Ideal Proof System that simulates all known semi-algebraic systems by representing sum-of-squares proofs as algebraic circuits over the reals.

Question: What is known about the polynomial equivalence between IPS and CPS?
Answer: The polynomial equivalence between IPS and CPS holds over both the integers and the rationals if and only if IPS admits polynomial-size refutations of the binary value principle for systems with no zero-one solutions.
style_catechism.coling::0a6f4d1d-1792-4bfc-a4cf-9fcf0636:
What can be said regarding phylogenetic networks?
Phylogenetic networks are leaf-labelled directed acyclic graphs that are used to describe non-treelike evolutionary histories and are thus a generalization of phylogenetic trees.

What can be said regarding the hybridization number?
The hybridization number of a phylogenetic network is the sum of all indegrees minus the number of nodes plus one.

What can be said regarding the Hybridization Number problem?
The Hybridization Number problem takes as input a collection of phylogenetic trees and asks to construct a phylogenetic network that contains an embedding of each of the input trees and has a smallest possible hybridization number.

What can be said regarding the algorithm for three binary phylogenetic trees?
The algorithm for three binary phylogenetic trees on n leaves runs in time O(c^k poly(n)), with k the hybridization number of an optimal network and c some positive constant.

What can be said regarding historical algorithm running times?
Historical algorithm running times show that for two trees, an algorithm running in time O(3.18^k n) was proposed before, whereas an algorithm running in time O(c^k poly(n)) for more than two trees had prior to this article remained elusive.

What can be said regarding agreement forests and topological search?
Agreement forests and topological search differ because the two-tree algorithm uses the close connection to acyclic agreement forests to achieve a linear exponent in running time, whereas previous algorithms for more than two trees relied on brute force search through underlying network topologies, yielding running times not O(c^k poly(n)) for any c.

What can be said regarding reconstruction challenges and novel structural results?
Reconstruction challenges and novel structural results arise because the agreement forest connection is weaker for more than two trees, making reconstruction challenging; however, we prove novel structural results allowing network reconstruction without guessing the topology.

What can be said regarding generalizability and the main open problem?
Generalizability and the main open problem show that our techniques generalize to more than three input trees except for one key lemma mapping network nodes to tree nodes to minimize guessing, making establishing such a mapping for more than three trees the main open problem.
style_catechism.coling::a098aa01-9d81-40a6-8321-ca3d4a88:
Can you explain the primary role of graph-Laplacians and spectral embeddings?
The primary role of graph-Laplacians and spectral embeddings is important across multiple machine learning domains, focusing primarily on graph-Laplacian dimension reduction for spectral clustering while remaining applicable in data mining and data manifold learning.

Can you explain how spectral embedding simplifies data processing?
How spectral embedding simplifies data processing is by providing a low-dimensional parametrization of the data manifold, making subsequent tasks like clustering with k-means or its approximations much easier.

Can you explain the major computational bottlenecks associated with large datasets?
The major computational bottlenecks associated with large datasets stem from two factors: computing the partial eigendecomposition of the graph-Laplacian typically requires a large Krylov subspace, and post-embedding operations must still process the full original number of data points, ruining efficiency.

Can you explain the drawbacks of using k-means relaxations on embedded data?
The drawbacks of using k-means relaxations on embedded data involve poor computational scaling relative to dataset size and a tendency to get stuck in local minima, making robustness dependent on the initial guess.

Can you explain the novel strategy introduced in this work?
The novel strategy introduced in this work switches the main focus from the entire dataset to a small subset of graph vertices, termed the target subset.

Can you explain the main capability of the two newly developed algorithms?
The main capability of the two newly developed algorithms is providing a low-dimensional representation of the original graph that accurately preserves important global distances between nodes in the target subset.

Can you explain how consistency with full-dataset spectral clustering is maintained?
How consistency with full-dataset spectral clustering is maintained is through a properly parametrized reduced-order model (ROM) of the graph-Laplacian that accurately approximates the original graph's diffusion transfer function for inputs and outputs restricted to the target subset.

Can you explain the operational benefits of focusing on a target subset?
The operational benefits of focusing on a target subset include significantly reducing the required Krylov subspace dimension and allowing conventional algorithms, such as k-means approximations, to run when they are most robust and efficient, a result confirmed through numerical experiments on synthetic and real data.

Can you explain the transfer-function-data-driven utility of the proposed ROM approach?
The transfer-function-data-driven utility of the proposed ROM approach lies in its ability to operate in a purely data-driven manner, making it the only feasible solution for extremely large, directly inaccessible graphs.

Can you explain the four main practical applications of these algorithms?
The four main practical applications of these algorithms are: first, standalone representative subset clustering when handling the full graph is infeasible or unnecessary; second, quality control; third, reducing problem size to enable sophisticated semi-definite programming (SDP) based k-means approximations instead of standard Lloyd's algorithm; fourth, serving as building blocks for a multi-level divide-and-conquer algorithm for the full graph, to be reported in a separate article.
style_catechism.coling::d9b96a87-ee9b-46e9-995f-edfccd85:
Question: What can be stated about the core research problem?
Answer: The core research problem is designing [n, k] linear codes for distributed storage systems satisfying the (r, t)-Local Repair Property, where any t simultaneously failed nodes can be locally repaired, each with locality r.

Question: What can be stated about the code parameters?
Answer: The code parameters n, k, r, t are positive integers such that r <= k <= n and t <= n - k.

Question: What can be stated about the functional repair model?
Answer: The functional repair model means that the packet stored in each newcomer is not necessarily an exact copy of the lost data, but a symbol keeping the (r, t)-local repair property.

Question: What can be stated about the sequential repair approach?
Answer: The sequential repair approach means that the t newcomers are ordered in a proper sequence such that each newcomer can be repaired from live nodes and preceding newcomers.

Question: What can be stated about functional locally repairable codes?
Answer: Functional locally repairable codes, or (n, k, r, t)-FLRCs, are the most general class of LRCs and contain several subclasses reported in literature.

Question: What can be stated about the main objective of this paper?
Answer: The main objective of this paper is to optimize the storage overhead, or equivalently the code rate, of FLRCs.

Question: What can be stated about the derived lower bounds?
Answer: The derived lower bounds establish a lower bound on code length n given t in {2, 3} and any k, r, generalizing the rate bound for t = 2 and improving it for t = 3.

Question: What can be stated about the proposed exact LRC constructions?
Answer: The proposed exact LRC constructions achieve the (n, k, r, t)-FLRC length bound for t in {2, 3}, proving tightness, showing no gap between optimal length of functional and exact LRCs for certain parameters, and operating over the binary field for practical interest.
style_catechism.coling::60c879b9-6ebb-4551-8f22-52c6a144:
Can you provide details about the fundamental task of SLAM? The fundamental task of SLAM involves constructing a map of an agent's environment while localizing the agent within that map.

Can you provide details about dense SLAM algorithms? Dense SLAM algorithms perform reconstruction and localization at pixel granularity, which requires significant computing power and hinders deployment on low power devices.

Can you provide details about approximate computing in SLAM? Approximate computing in SLAM speeds up implementations as long as approximations allow the agent to navigate correctly through the environment.

Can you provide details about previous studies of approximation in SLAM? Previous studies of approximation in SLAM assumed the entire trajectory was known beforehand, focusing on offline controllers setting static knobs at start.

Can you provide details about dynamic knob settings in practice? Dynamic knob settings in practice offer opportunities to reduce computation time and energy because trajectories are usually unknown ahead of time.

Can you provide details about the SLAMBooster system? The SLAMBooster system is an application aware online control system for dense SLAM that adaptively controls approximation knobs during motion.

Can you provide details about pure PID controllers in SLAMBooster? Pure PID controllers in SLAMBooster proved application agnostic and caused an unacceptable reduction in localization accuracy.

Can you provide details about domain knowledge integration in SLAMBooster? Domain knowledge integration in SLAMBooster prevents accuracy loss by using smooth surface detection and pose correction.

Can you provide details about the evaluation of SLAMBooster? The evaluation of SLAMBooster was performed in SLAMBench using over a dozen trajectories from literature and custom studies.

Can you provide details about the experimental results for SLAMBooster? The experimental results for SLAMBooster demonstrate an average computation time reduction of 72 percent and energy savings of 35 percent on embedded platforms while maintaining localization accuracy within reasonable bounds, enabling deployment across wider device ranges.
style_catechism.coling::6b54ef51-f42e-4ac2-840e-6b536faa:
Question: Could you elaborate on the initiation of legislation in the European Union?
Answer: The initiation of legislation in the European Union is a legal monopoly belonging to the Commission, while the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union hold powers of amendment and veto during the process.

Question: Could you elaborate on the legal provisions regarding equality and democracy in the Treaties?
Answer: The legal provisions regarding equality and democracy in the Treaties are found in Articles 9 and 10 of the Treaty on European Union, stating that the Union observes citizen equality and representative democracy.

Question: Could you elaborate on the deficiencies of democracy and equality in practice?
Answer: The deficiencies of democracy and equality in practice manifest because parliamentary representatives cannot initiate legislation against Commission wishes, small country citizens have ten times the voting weight of large country citizens, and qualified majorities or Council consensus are required.

Question: Could you elaborate on the traditional justification for this democratic deficit?
Answer: The traditional justification for this democratic deficit under the Treaties is that economic and political integration required expert technical coordination while public understanding grew and post-war nationalism declined.

Question: Could you elaborate on the historical evolution of the European Parliament?
Answer: The historical evolution of the European Parliament saw it progress from an unelected assembly to direct elections in 1979 and gradually assume greater rights within the legislative process over time.

Question: Could you elaborate on citizens' democratic rights under TEU Article 11 and TFEU Article 227?
Answer: Citizens' democratic rights under TEU Article 11 and TFEU Article 227 include publicising views, submitting initiatives requiring one million signatures for Commission consideration, and petitioning Parliament on affecting issues, though these remain limited compared to national member state polities.

Question: Could you elaborate on the electoral framework for Members of the European Parliament?
Answer: The electoral framework for Members of the European Parliament requires elections every five years using proportional representation or single transferable vote systems across member states.

Question: Could you elaborate on degressive proportionality in parliamentary representation?
Answer: Degressive proportionality in parliamentary representation governs the distribution of the 750 seats according to state size, granting citizens of smaller member states greater relative voice than those in larger states, despite the Council representing states.

Question: Could you elaborate on political party groupings and legal rulings on party funding?
Answer: Political party groupings and legal rulings on party funding show MEPs dividing along political lines, with the European People's Party largest and European Socialists leading opposition, while the Court of Justice held in Les Verts that funding is regulated by member states.

Question: Could you elaborate on the supervisory mechanisms available to the Parliament?
Answer: The supervisory mechanisms available to the Parliament include calling inquiries into maladministration, appointing an Ombudsman, demanding Commission answers, holding consultation rights, and censuring the Commission by a two-thirds majority, as occurred in 1999.

Question: Could you elaborate on the ultimate distribution of legislative power in the Union?
Answer: The ultimate distribution of legislative power in the Union remains restricted because Parliament cannot pass legislation without the Commission and Council, meaning power (kratia) is not fully held by the people (demos), so administration is not yet in the hands of the many.
style_catechism.coling::049da962-b4ab-4271-80d7-6c08dd71:
What is known regarding Martin Luther's adherence to traditional Marian decrees?
Martin Luther's adherence to traditional Marian decrees is widely acknowledged by theologians who agree that, despite his harsh polemics against Roman Catholic opponents over Mary and the saints, he maintained belief in church dogmas, ecumenical councils, Mary's perpetual virginity, and her status as the Theotokos or Mother of God.

What is known regarding Luther's position on the Immaculate Conception?
Luther's position on the Immaculate Conception remains debated; special attention notes he firmly adhered to this view three hundred years before Pope Pius IX dogmatized it in 1854, while others maintain he later changed his stance on this then undefined doctrine while still holding to Mary's lifelong sinlessness.

What is known regarding Luther's changing stance on the Assumption?
Luther's changing stance on the Assumption meant it was an understood fact early in his life, but he later observed that scripture said nothing about it and subsequently discontinued celebrating its feast day, though he retained the firm conviction that Mary and the saints live on after death.

What is known regarding Luther's preaching career concerning Marian devotion?
Luther's preaching career concerning Marian devotion spans his work as a priest, professor, and reformer who preached, taught, and argued about Mary with a verbosity ranging from childlike piety to sophisticated polemics, views intimately linked to his Christocentric theology and its consequences for liturgy and piety.

What is known regarding Luther's critique of Roman Catholic practices?
Luther's critique of Roman Catholic practices targeted Papists for blurring the boundary between admiring divine grace in humans and offering religious service to creatures, leading him to view celebrating saints' days and addressing intercessory prayers to Mary and departed saints as idolatry.

What is known regarding Luther's final thoughts on Marian veneration?
Luther's final thoughts on Marian veneration are historically preserved in a sermon that he preached at Wittenberg merely one month prior to his death.
style_catechism.coling::0b4651e6-8f56-467b-81ae-810fa781:
What can you tell me about a digital signature?
A digital signature is a mathematical scheme for verifying the authenticity of digital messages or documents. A valid digital signature, where prerequisites are satisfied, gives a recipient very high confidence that the message was created by a known sender, proving authenticity, and was not altered in transit, proving integrity.

What can you tell me about the applications of digital signatures?
The applications of digital signatures include being a standard element of cryptographic protocol suites. They are commonly used for software distribution, financial transactions, contract management software, and other cases where detecting forgery or tampering is important.

What can you tell me about electronic signatures?
Electronic signatures include any electronic data carrying the intent of a signature, but not all electronic signatures use digital signatures. Digital signatures often implement electronic signatures, which carry legal significance in Canada, South Africa, the United States, Algeria, Turkey, India, Brazil, Indonesia, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Switzerland, Chile, and the European Union.

What can you tell me about asymmetric cryptography in digital signatures?
Asymmetric cryptography in digital signatures provides validation and security over non-secure channels. Properly implemented, a digital signature gives the receiver reason to believe the message was sent by the claimed sender. Digital signatures are equivalent to handwritten signatures in many respects, but are more difficult to forge. These cryptographically based schemes must be properly implemented to be effective.

What can you tell me about non-repudiation in digital signatures?
Non-repudiation in digital signatures means signers cannot successfully claim they did not sign a message while claiming their private key remains secret. Further, some non-repudiation schemes offer a timestamp, keeping the signature valid even if the private key is exposed.

What can you tell me about digitally signed messages?
Digitally signed messages may be anything representable as a bitstring. Examples include electronic mail, contracts, or messages sent via other cryptographic protocols.
style_catechism.coling::203e204e-a867-4d1d-97e8-bdd789e6:
What can you tell me about the basic definition of speech recognition?
The basic definition of speech recognition refers to an interdisciplinary subfield of computer science and computational linguistics developing methodologies and technologies that enable the recognition and translation of spoken language into text by computers with the main benefit of searchability.

What can you tell me about alternative names and related disciplines of speech recognition?
Alternative names and related disciplines of speech recognition include automatic speech recognition, computer speech recognition, or speech to text. It incorporates knowledge and research in computer science, linguistics, and computer engineering, while the reverse process is speech synthesis.

What can you tell me about training processes and system categories in speech recognition?
Training processes and system categories in speech recognition involve enrollment where an individual reads text or isolated vocabulary into the system. The system analyzes the person's specific voice to fine-tune recognition for increased accuracy. Systems using training are speaker-dependent, while systems without training are speaker-independent.

What can you tell me about practical applications of speech recognition systems?
Practical applications of speech recognition systems include voice user interfaces such as voice dialing, call routing, domotic appliance control, search key words in podcasts, simple data entry, preparation of structured radiology reports, determining speaker characteristics, speech-to-text processing, and aircraft direct voice input.

What can you tell me about voice recognition and speaker identification?
Voice recognition and speaker identification refers to identifying the speaker rather than what they are saying. Recognizing the speaker simplifies the task of translating speech in systems trained on a specific voice, or authenticates and verifies speaker identity for security processes.

What can you tell me about technological progress and industry adoption in speech recognition?
Technological progress and industry adoption in speech recognition features a long history of innovations, recently driven by deep learning and big data. Advances are shown by surging academic papers and worldwide industry adoption of deep learning methods in designing and deploying systems.
style_catechism.coling::9be05dd7-05a8-4b0e-a617-ae611f4d:
Could you provide details about the definition of control theory?
The definition of control theory is a field of mathematics dealing with the control of dynamical systems in engineered processes and machines.

Could you provide details about the primary objective of control theory?
The primary objective of control theory is to develop a model or algorithm governing system inputs to drive a system to a desired state, while minimizing delay, overshoot, or steady-state error and ensuring control stability, often aiming to achieve optimality.

Could you provide details about the required controller?
The required controller must possess corrective behavior, monitoring the controlled process variable and comparing it with the reference or set point.

Could you provide details about the error signal?
The error signal, also called SP-PV error, is the difference between the actual and desired value of the process variable, applied as feedback to generate a control action bringing the variable to the set point.

Could you provide details about controllability and observability?
Controllability and observability are other key aspects that are studied within control theory.

Could you provide details about applications in control system engineering?
Applications in control system engineering involve designing automation that has revolutionized manufacturing, aircraft, communications, and other industries, while creating fields like robotics.

Could you provide details about the block diagram and transfer function?
The block diagram and transfer function involve extensive use of diagrammatic models where the transfer function, also known as system function or network function, models input-output relations via differential equations.

Could you provide details about the origins of control theory?
The origins of control theory date from the 19th century, when the theoretical basis for operating governors was first described by James Clerk Maxwell.

Could you provide details about contributors to control stability criteria?
Contributors to control stability criteria include Edward Routh in 1874, Charles Sturm, Adolf Hurwitz in 1895, and Nicolas Minorsky, who developed PID control theory from 1922 onwards.

Could you provide details about broader applications of control theory?
Broader applications of control theory exist because, as the general theory of feedback systems, it is useful wherever feedback occurs—including life sciences, computer engineering, sociology, and operations research.
style_catechism.coling::5293d27b-2991-4ca1-93ab-e336d0eb:
Can you provide information about the definition of drug design? The definition of drug design, often called rational drug design or rational design, refers to the inventive process of finding new medications based on knowledge of a biological target.

Can you provide information about the primary role of the drug molecule? The primary role of the drug molecule, which is most commonly an organic small molecule, involves activating or inhibiting the function of a biomolecule such as a protein to produce a therapeutic benefit for the patient.

Can you provide information about the fundamental principle of molecular binding? The fundamental principle of molecular binding requires designing molecules that are complementary in shape and charge to the biomolecular target with which they interact.

Can you provide information about computer-aided drug design? Computer-aided drug design is the application of computer modeling techniques during the drug design process.

Can you provide information about structure-based drug design? Structure-based drug design is a specific type of drug design that relies directly on knowledge of the three-dimensional structure of the biomolecular target.

Can you provide information about biopharmaceuticals in modern drug discovery? Biopharmaceuticals in modern drug discovery, including peptides and therapeutic antibodies, represent an increasingly important class of drugs alongside small molecules, with computational methods developed to enhance their affinity, selectivity, and stability.

Can you provide information about the terminology misnomer of drug design? The terminology misnomer of drug design stems from the fact that ligand design is a more accurate term, describing the design of a molecule that will bind tightly to its intended target.

Can you provide information about additional properties required for drug efficacy? Additional properties required for drug efficacy include bioavailability, metabolic half-life, and minimal side effects, all of which must be optimized beyond basic binding affinity before a ligand becomes a safe and efficacious medication.

Can you provide information about early candidate selection strategies? Early candidate selection strategies focus on predicting physicochemical properties to reduce high attrition rates during clinical development, making an approved marketed drug more likely.

Can you provide information about early drug discovery screening techniques? Early drug discovery screening techniques combine in vitro experiments with computational methods to select candidate compounds exhibiting favorable ADME and toxicological profiles.
style_catechism.coling::d2400f57-c1e4-49a6-aaa9-1c92f181:
What can you explain regarding data dredging?
Data dredging, also known as data snooping or p-hacking, is the misuse of data analysis to find patterns in data that can be presented as statistically significant, thus dramatically increasing and understating the risk of false positives.

What can you explain regarding the execution of data dredging?
The execution of data dredging is accomplished by performing many statistical tests on the data and only reporting those specific tests that come back with significant results.

What can you explain regarding the methodology of data dredging?
The methodology of data dredging involves testing multiple hypotheses using a single data set by exhaustively searching for combinations of variables showing correlation or groups of observations displaying differences in their mean values.

What can you explain regarding conventional tests of statistical significance?
Conventional tests of statistical significance are based on the probability that a particular result would arise if chance alone were at work, necessarily accepting some risk of mistaken conclusions like mistaken rejections of the null hypothesis.

What can you explain regarding the effect of performing large numbers of tests?
The effect of performing large numbers of tests is that some produce false results by chance alone; for example, five percent of randomly chosen hypotheses might be erroneously reported to be statistically significant at the five percent level.

What can you explain regarding the consequence of testing enough hypotheses?
The consequence of testing enough hypotheses is that it is virtually certain some will be reported to be statistically significant, since almost every dataset with randomness contains spurious correlations, misleading researchers using data mining techniques if they are not cautious.

What can you explain regarding the multiple comparisons problem in data dredging?
The multiple comparisons problem in data dredging is disregarded when researchers fail to alert the reader to the total number of subgroup comparisons examined when comparing different subgroups.
style_catechism.coling::5e64f27a-ba00-4d66-8985-34fc48e8:
What should you know about handling a mother who acts mean because of her insecurities? Handling a mother who acts mean because of her insecurities means remembering that although you wish she were sweet, gentle, understanding, and kind, you must never be disrespectful. Do not verbalize your feelings in front of her, because that will only make things worse. There is a very good chance she knows she is not smart, which causes her mean behavior, so reminding her of her shortcomings will not make your life easier.

What should you know about practicing emotional detachment from your mother? Practicing emotional detachment from your mother involves giving yourself permission to cry, yell, or scream, and then stepping away from your emotions. Detachment is one of the most constructive ways to deal with her: show no anger, whining, crying, begging, yelling, or belittling, but rely strictly on facts. If she intentionally tries to hurt or anger you, your best defense is not letting yourself feel hurt or angry.

What should you know about doing what your mother wants before she asks? Doing what your mother wants before she asks gives her one less thing to be mean about, while giving you the upper hand when asking for what you want.

What should you know about seeking outside advice from healthier adults? Seeking outside advice from healthier adults requires paying close attention to friends' mothers who are more gentle, consistent, and responsible. Get outside information, since much of what you are told daily is sabotaging and wrong. Instead of just getting mad at her for steering you wrong, seek better sources like ministers, therapists, teachers, and healthier adults, comparing her words against theirs to break generational cycles.

What should you know about studying family dynamics to build inner resistance? Studying family dynamics to build inner resistance can be done through books to help you understand the family dynamic and choose your path. Not responding to mind games in the usual way may make her angrier, but building inner resistance is important to protect your mind and soul.

What should you know about responding to accusations from a cruel mother? Responding to accusations from a cruel mother means not being surprised if you get accused of things you would never think of doing, since she expects you to do whatever she does. Cruel mothers lack a good grip on reality and cannot distinguish between good and bad behavior. Behave well anyway and spend time with others so they can see the situation.
